review_findings.diff: One commit, one file (llvm/lib/Target/RISCV/RISCVInstrInfoXpulp.td, already fork-owned). The subject is the exact insn-tablegen cluster subject. Trailers are Change-Note: 20/F008.md and Task. Every hunk serves the root cause: two new ImmLeaf leaves, the new clipu_idiom PatFrags, getZExtValue->getSExtValue in the clip predicate, and the two idiom Pats switched to the new leaves/fragment. Nothing is deleted. The old TImmLeaf defs and betweenu are kept because the builtin patterns (:1874/:1878) and the p.clipur Pat still use them. No test is edited. No new early return and no forced condition.
review_findings.rule8_provenance: Pre-existing fork defect. `git log pulp/integer_SIMD_fix -S'def betweenu' -- llvm/lib/Target/RISCV/` gives f1b7aebff8c2 '[LLVM/PULP/SNITCH] Support for PULP and Snitch cores/platforms' (Ficarelli, 2022-08-25). toolchains/ref-18 clang emits no p.clip/p.clipu for logs/20-F008-v2/clamps.c, so the defect is confirmed as pre-existing. The upstream reference (llvmorg-20.1.8 RISCVInstrInfoXCV.td:723 `powerOf2Minus1 : ImmLeaf<XLenVT, isPowerOf2_32(Imm+1)>`, :724 trailing1sPlus1, :771-773 PatCoreVAluGprImm) matches the note. Upstream uses these only for the intrinsic. The idiom fragments are fork-only, as the note says. The fork's leaf is stricter than upstream (it caps the bound so the field stays <= 31; upstream would accept 2^31-1 and produce field 32), which is correct.
review_findings.immediate_leaves: Checked by hand and empirically. powerOf2Minus1_imm_pulp accepts exactly {2^k-1 : 0<=k<=30}: Imm is the sign-extended i32, isUInt<30> rejects negatives and >=2^30, and isPowerOf2_32(Imm+1) rejects non-masks. negativePowerOf2_imm accepts exactly {-2^k : 0<=k<=30}: INT_MIN gives 2^31, which fails the <= 2^30 test, and positive i32 values never make -Imm a u32 power of two. The clip predicate with getSExtValue forces lo == ~hi, so a p.clip match is exactly [-2^(n-1), 2^(n-1)-1] for n in 1..31, and trailing1sPlus1_pulp gives the field n. p.clipu gives [0, 2^(n-1)-1] -> field n, for n in 1..31. GVSoC pulp_v2.hpp:1930 p_clipi_exec is low=-(1<<(imm-1)), high=(1<<(imm-1))-1, and :1940 p_clipui_exec is high=(1<<(imm-1))-1 with lib_CLIPU (int.h:1305, signed: a>high -> high, a<=0 -> 0). Field 31 is well defined there (1<<30).
review_findings.gcc_encoding_comparison: My own sweep of all 31 widths (caps.c: c_n=[-2^(n-1),2^(n-1)-1], u_n=[0,2^(n-1)-1]) against GAP9 GCC -march=rv32imcxgap9 -O2 gives the same field for every n from 3 to 30, for both p.clip and p.clipu. The encoding words are also the same (p.clip a0,a0,8 = 0x14851533, p.clipu a0,a0,9 = 0x14952533, p.clip 16 = 0x15051533, p.clipu 17 = 0x15152533). Differences: n=1/2, where LLVM emits the equivalent srai a0,a0,31 or sgtz (both correct on GVSoC). n=31, where GCC stops at field 30 and uses lui/min/max, but this build emits p.clip/p.clipu 31. Field 31 is verified correct on GVSoC (s30/u30 in sim_clamp, plus random seeds with n=31). It is a legal 5-bit field, but GCC never emits it, so GAP9 silicon behaviour for field 31 rests on the GVSoC model alone. Non-blocking.
review_findings.clipu_signedness: Correct. p.clipu is a signed clamp to [0,hi] (lib_CLIPU). clipu_idiom matches smin(smax(x,0),hi) and smax(smin(x,hi),0) (identical for hi>=0) and umin(smax(x,0),hi), which is the same value because smax(x,0)>=0 and hi<=2^30-1. It does not match smax(umin(x,hi),0) or umin/umax-only forms, which are not equivalent. The unsigned-only clamp `(unsigned)x>255?255:x` stays p.minu (verified).

review_findings.clipr_preexisting_finding: Confirmed, and confirmed as pre-existing. logs/20-F008-v2/clipr/k.c (rc(x,b)=min(max(x,~b),b)) with m.c (b=-5), rebuilt and run on GVSoC by me. build/int-20 and build/20-F008 both emit the identical `p.clipr a0,a0,a1` (0x14b55533) and give 5/8 mismatches (x in {-100,-6,-5,0,3} gives 4, expected -5). GAP9 GCC emits not+p.max+p.min and gives 0 mismatches. toolchains/ref-18 also emits p.clipr for rc, so the miscompile dates back to f1b7aebff8c2 and is not introduced or changed by F008 (the P_CLIPR Pat line is untouched by the diff). Mechanism: with b<0, p.clipr's low=-b-1 > high=b, and lib_CLIP returns low for x<low, while the C expression always returns b. This deserves a backlog entry (a real wrong-result bug, arguably above P2), as the worker proposes. The dead p.clipur idiom (umax(x,0) folds away) is also correctly reported as latent.
non_blocking_notes: The clip PatFrag predicate (unchanged apart from Z->S) reads N->getOperand(0)->getOperand(1) at fixed positions. If TableGen's commuted variant ever matched with the constant as operand 0 of the outer smin/smax, it would index a ConstantSDNode child. That is unreachable in practice because SelectionDAG::getNode canonicalises constants to the RHS of commutative smin/smax. Before this change the pattern could not match at all, so the case is now theoretically reachable. A future cleanup could guard with N->getOperand(0)->getNumOperands() == 2.
